source_name: Portal javnih naročil (Uradni list RS) — main portal
why_relevant: Statutory national publication point under ZJN-3 art. 52 for all contract notices, award notices, corrections and contract-modification notices by Slovenian contracting authorities, including bank account services, cash handling, POS/ATM, card issuing and payment gateway procurements. Operated by Javno podjetje Uradni list RS d.o.o. on behalf of the Ministry of Public Administration.

source_name: Portal javnih naročil — Pregled objav (notice search / browse by CPV, buyer, supplier, date)
source_subtype: notice search interface with parameterised URLs
why_relevant: The actual queryable index behind the portal. Observed URL pattern encodes filters (e.g. ?f=ponudnik:<matična št>|datum:YYYY,M,D-|cpv:66), which makes deterministic CPV-scoped and supplier-scoped harvesting of banking/payments notices feasible — including tracking which bank or PSP won which authority.

source_name: e-JN — Elektronsko javno naročanje (national e-tendering system)
why_relevant: The statutory system in which Slovenian tender procedures are actually run (bid submission, e-Dossier, e-Auction). Publishes the current live tender list and the operational rules; the counterpart to the notice portal and the place where documentation and deadlines live.

source_name: e-JN 'Aktualna javna naročila' live tender list
why_relevant: Machine-friendly-ish list of currently open procedures with authority name, procurement name/ID, publication date, submission deadline and status — the earliest structured signal that a banking/payments tender is live and still biddable.

source_name: eNaročanje notice form pages (individual published notice objects)
why_relevant: Stable per-notice permalink pattern (Obrazci/?id_obrazec=NNNNN) containing the full structured notice body: subject, CPV, estimated value, procedure type, criteria, and for award notices the winning bidder and contract value. This is the atomic record the whole A2 workstream needs.

source_name: Uradni list Republike Slovenije (official gazette)
why_relevant: Publisher/operator of the procurement portal and the official gazette itself; carries the legal instruments (ZJN-3 and amendments, thresholds, implementing rules) plus announcements of portal redesigns and new e-forms that change the data schema our collectors depend on.

source_name: ZJN-3 — Zakon o javnem naročanju (consolidated text, PISRS)
why_relevant: Defines what must be published, by whom, in what form and within what deadlines (e.g. award notice within 30 days of contract conclusion), and how banking/financial service contract values are estimated (on the basis of fees/commissions). This is the ground truth for interpreting completeness and for detecting when a notice is missing.

source_name: Direktorat za javno naročanje (Ministry of Public Administration)
why_relevant: System owner of e-JN. Publishes guidance, FAQ, framework-agreement and joint-procurement programmes (skupna javna naročila), and the annual statistical reports — the place where centralised state-level banking/payment contracts would be announced before they hit the portal.

source_name: Statist — public procurement statistics application (OPSI)
why_relevant: Comprehensive published data on public procurement awarded in Slovenia from 1.1.2013 onward: contracting authority (name, region), procedure (subject, legal basis, procedure type) and bidder (name, country, region). Gives a structured, back-fillable time series of who wins banking/payments contracts, without scraping every notice.

source_name: OPSI — Evidenca javnih naročil dataset (CKAN)
why_relevant: Machine-readable register of public procurements on the national open-data portal, served by CKAN with an API — the cheapest reliable bulk route into the same notice stream the portal publishes.

source_name: Annual statistical reports on awarded public contracts (Zbirka letnih statističnih poročil)
why_relevant: Ministry-prepared, government-confirmed annual aggregates under ZJN-3/ZJNPOV. Useful for sizing the addressable public-sector banking/payments spend and for sanity-checking notice-level collection coverage year over year.

source_name: Državna revizijska komisija (DKOM) — decisions database and search
why_relevant: Independent review body for procurement legality. Its published decisions reveal contested banking/payments tenders, the technical and financial requirements that were challenged, bidder identities, and cancelled or annulled procedures — information that never appears in the neutral notice text. Also an early warning that a tender will be delayed or re-run.

source_name: ERAR (KPK) — public money transaction transparency application
why_relevant: Reported to hold on the order of 131 million transactions of public-sector bodies for the last ~10 years, plus e-invoice data from September 2024. Lets us see actual payments from public bodies to named banks, card processors and terminal vendors — revealing incumbency and real contract run-rates even where no award notice was published (below-threshold buys).

source_name: TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) — Slovenian above-threshold notices
why_relevant: Mandatory EU-level mirror of Slovenian above-threshold notices, in standardised eForms with a documented v3 search API — structurally easier to harvest than the national portal and multilingual. Confirmed to carry Slovenian banking-services awards under CPV 66110000 (e.g. an Aerodrom Ljubljana/Brnik banking services award to SKB d.d.).

source_name: UL info tok (Uradni list RS commercial tender-monitoring service)
why_relevant: Run by the portal's own operator; monitors Slovenian portal notices plus TED, with CPV-code-based alerting. Valuable as a coverage benchmark and as a fallback alerting channel, and its help/FAQ pages document the portal's own notice taxonomy authoritatively.

source_name: Javnirazpisi.com — tender aggregator and CPV reference
why_relevant: Claims to sweep 4000+ sources of javna naročila and javni razpisi beyond the national portal (bulletins, newspapers, individual authority websites), so its coverage map points to publication channels our cell would otherwise miss. Also hosts a usable Slovenian CPV-code reference for building the banking/payments code list.

source_name: Monitor obvestil o javnih naročilih (informator-javnihrazpisov.si)
why_relevant: A second independent Slovenian notice-monitoring service. Useful as a cross-check on whether our own harvest of the portal is complete, and as a discovery route to authorities publishing outside the main portal.

source_name: openprocurements.com — Slovenia CPV-sliced tender mirror
why_relevant: Third-party mirror that exposes Slovenian notices sliced by CPV code in clean, stable URL paths (observed: /cpv/66510000/ for insurance services), which makes it a convenient secondary index for CPV division 66 (financial and insurance services) and a validation set against our primary harvest.

source_name: TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) — notice search, EN interface
why_relevant: Official EU Supplement to the Official Journal (OJ S). Every above-threshold Slovenian banking/payments contract notice and contract award notice must appear here, CPV-coded and with an English version. Primary EU-level channel for the SI cell; filterable by country=Slovenia and CPV (66100000, 66110000, 66172000, 30144200).

source_name: TED — Slovenian-language interface (/sl)
why_relevant: Same notice corpus rendered in Slovenian, so notice titles/objects appear with the native procurement vocabulary (javno naročilo, obvestilo o oddaji naročila, bančne storitve, plačilni promet, bankomat). Useful for building the SI glossary and for matching TED notices back to national enarocanje.si records.

source_name: TED Search API (api.ted.europa.eu, v3)
why_relevant: Machine-readable, anonymous-access query interface over all published TED notices. Supports expert queries (country, CPV, notice type, publication date) and bulk retrieval of notice XML. This is the single highest-leverage collection route for the whole A2 workstream at EU level.

source_name: TED Developer Docs (docs.ted.europa.eu) — API and Open Data Service guides
why_relevant: Authoritative documentation for query syntax, field names, eForms field IDs, pagination and versioning. Required to write correct CPV/country expert queries and to keep the collector working across TED API versions.

source_name: TED bulk XML packages (daily and monthly editions)
why_relevant: Full historical corpus of OJ S notices as XML, monthly collections reported back to 2011 and an FTP archive reported back to 1993. Enables a one-off backfill of all Slovenian banking/payments notices rather than incremental-only collection.
